title: SimpleKorean: Short, clear Korean from AI
description: SimpleKorean is an agent skill that makes AI write documents and replies in simple Korean. It splits long sentences, removes translationese, and keeps the spelling of terms the same. It works in Claude Code, Codex, and Python.

lead:
SimpleKorean is an agent skill. It makes AI write documents and replies in simple Korean.
It splits long sentences, removes translationese, and keeps the spelling of terms the same.
It takes ideas from SimpleEnglish and ASD-STE100.
ex_title: See how the same draft changes
ex_sub: The left side is the original draft. The right side is the document with SimpleKorean. Under each changed sentence, we name the rule that changed it. The example text stays in Korean.
note_heading: Use a heading, not bold text and an em-dash
note_firewall: Join words with a particle, not a middle dot. Use the simple present
note_host: Name the host that runs the command. Change the advice ending to the command form "-하세요"
note_particle: Join words with "과" and "와" (and), not a middle dot
note_moved: Moved to sentence 6 on the right, without the advice ending
ex_foot: Source: evals/results/2026-10-21. A person matched the sentences and named the rules. For more comparisons, see the before-and-after examples.
b_title: What changes when the skill is on
b_sub: We publish the raw outputs that we measured. You can calculate the numbers below again from those outputs.
m1_desc: Defects that readers see, in 32 replies. We count em-dashes, bold text, tables, and a header or list on the first line.
m2_desc: Pairs out of 16 where the judge chose the SimpleKorean reply without knowing which it was. 3 pairs were ties and 1 pair was a loss.
m3_desc: Linter warnings per 100 eojeol. An eojeol is a unit of Korean text between two spaces.
m4_desc: The longest sentence in 16 documents. In strict mode, it is 13 eojeol.
b_foot:
claude-sonnet-5-5 wrote the documents and replies. claude-opus-5-5 was the judge.
The judge is also Claude, so it can favor models of the same family.
r_sub: The rules split long sentences, remove formatting that is not necessary, and fix translationese.
r1: Put the answer in the first sentence
r1_before: An opening that repeats the question
r2: Do not use bold text or tables
r3_before: Thoughts that are only half joined
r4: Write procedures in 15 eojeol or fewer, and descriptions in 20 eojeol or fewer
r4_before: Long sentences that do not end
r5: Put conditions before the command with "-면" (if)
r5_before: "단, ~경우" (however, in case of ~) after the command, which the reader sees too late
r6: Use the active voice and simple tenses
r7: Do not use guessing or advice endings
r8: Give one word only one meaning
r_foot: The rules come from ASD-STE100, the controlled English for aircraft maintenance documents. The full rules are in SKILL.md.
s_sub: The skill follows the Korean loanword spelling rules and the examples of the National Institute of Korean Language. When no official spelling exists, the project chooses one.
s_foot: If your company uses a different spelling, change it in .simple-korean.json at the top of your repository.
